customManagers.description: Track the pinned dotfiles commit that the debug/dev/dev-lite images clone. Without a pin the image content depends on whatever dotfiles HEAD is at build time, so builds aren't reproducible and a bad dotfiles push reaches every image built after it.

Track version pins declared as build args. Renovate's dockerfile manager only reads FROM lines, so an ARG <NAME>_VERSION is invisible to it and would never move. Each pin declares its own datasource in a preceding '# renovate:' comment.

packageRules.description: Everything the customManagers pick up out of an active image's Dockerfile lands as 'build', matching how base image bumps are committed, so release-please cuts a patch release for the affected image. Listed first so the more specific rules below can refine it.

Base image bumps for released images land as 'build' so release-please cuts a patch release for the affected image. Digests are pinned (index/manifest-list digest, so multi-arch builds still resolve per-platform) - upstream rebuilds a floating tag like debian:13 without changing the tag string, and only a digest bump catches that.
Templates aren't built/released by this pipeline (no release-please package exists for docker/templates/**) - keep them updated without implying a release is needed.

Every image cloning dotfiles moves together in a single PR - the pin exists to make builds reproducible, not to let images drift apart from one another. 'build' so each affected image still gets its patch release. Run shell/bump-dotfiles-ref.sh to do the same bump by hand.
Deprecated legacy images are not released anymore, skip churn.
